title: Deploying and operating a contract
method: Two public web searches (official docs domain); one opened primary documentation page. No calls to networks, RPCs, wallets, proof services, or deployment tools.
authority: Official Midnight documentation; authoritative for the documented Midnight.js and Compact deployment workflow, not evidence of Sherlock/custom-ZKIR compatibility or operator-specific setup.
precise_locators: The transaction pipeline and its providers, lines 65-75
Promoting a deployment to Preprod, lines 700-722

falsifiable_source_claims: The guide identifies local, Preprod, Preview, and Mainnet network IDs and describes promoting its local deployment to Preprod by changing configuration and funding a wallet.

The guide assigns separate roles to privateStateProvider, publicDataProvider, zkConfigProvider, proofProvider, walletProvider, and midnightProvider; the ZK config provider reads prover/verifier keys and ZKIR artifacts from compile output, while proofProvider sends requests to a proof server.

The guide’s local verification checks deployment, circuit-call txId and blockHeight, and indexer-decoded contract state; its separate chain observation section tests block-header subscription and extrinsic/event extraction.
limitations: The examples use a Compact bulletin-board contract and do not show a custom ZKIR route.
The page does not identify a network called stagenet or establish Sherlock operator configuration.
It does not specify EffectStream semantics or prove effect-prefix correspondence.
